final_answer:
Depth-first search (DFS) and breadth-first search (BFS) are both algorithms used to traverse or search through a graph. DFS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, making it suitable for problems where the solution is likely to be deep in the graph. BFS, on the other hand, explores all neighbors at the current depth level before moving to the next level, ensuring the shortest path is found in unweighted graphs. 

You would choose DFS when memory is limited or when you need to explore paths deeply, such as in maze-solving or puzzles. BFS is preferred when finding the shortest path in an unweighted graph or when the solution is likely to be close to the root node. Safe.
